issues.issue: The representation is expressly cut down to "such limited scope of disclosure" as would be required were the Insurer not the registrant, a self-defining limit with no ascertainable content. What the Insurer actually warrants about the Insurer Information depends on that undefined boundary.

The confidentiality undertaking is excepted where disclosure is "requested by appropriate governmental authorities" or "as necessary to preserve its rights or security under or to enforce the Operative Documents" — exceptions requiring no compulsion and defined by the Insurer's own judgment. The carve-outs are broad enough to be argued to swallow the covenant.

The Insurer's compliance representation is tested by whether a violation "could result in a Material Adverse Change with respect to the Insurer", but Section 1.01 defines that term by reference to ability to perform "under any of the Operative Documents", and the Policy is not among the Operative Documents listed there. The Insurer's principal obligation therefore falls outside the very test the provision uses.

The Insurer need only "use commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain its accountants' consent letter, with no benchmark and no consequence stated if the letter is not obtained. The undefined effort standard governs the Depositor's ability to make its Regulation AB filings.

The representation is framed by reference to reports required "pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act", a term not defined in Article I, which defines only "Securities Exchange Act". The same sentence then reverts to "the Securities Exchange Act", leaving the two labels to be reconciled.

The trigger includes "if the representation in Section 2.05(i) is no longer true", but Section 2.05(i) is the Insurer's consent to incorporation by reference and contains no representation; the representation is in Section 2.05(j), which itself points forward to this subsection. The misdirected cross-reference makes the condition for furnishing financial statements uncertain.

This subsection is where "Insurer Financial Statements" is actually defined, yet Section 1.01 states the term "has the meaning assigned to such term in Section 2.03() below". The definition and its stated source cannot be reconciled.

The Insurer must disclose affiliations only "to the extent actually known and material", with no inquiry duty and no materiality benchmark, and its deadline runs from a filing date the Depositor merely "has stated" in its own certificate. Both the content and the timing of the obligation are set by undefined standards.

The Insurer agrees to comply with "all reasonable requests" for information "necessary for the Depositor to comply with Item 1114", without identifying Item 1114 of Regulation AB or bounding what information is necessary. The obligation's scope rests entirely on the undefined word "reasonable".

The no-affiliation representation ends with the garbled qualifier "without regard to affiliations by common control-with the Insurer", which either excludes common-control affiliates from the representation or does the opposite. That carve-out determines the entire content of the representation.

The Section 3.01 chapeau has the Insurer agreeing "to issue the Policy on the Closing Date subject to satisfaction of the conditions precedent", while the recitals state that "the Insurer has issued the Policy" and the Policy itself is dated the same day. Whether the Policy was conditional on these deliveries or already unconditionally issued is a recital-versus-operative conflict.

The condition is satisfied only by documents "in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Insurer", a purely subjective standard with no objective referent. What suffices is measured only by the Insurer's own view.

The condition covers representations "set forth or incorporated by reference in this Insurance Agreement", which by Section 2.01(n) means every representation in every Operative Document, without any materiality qualifier. How far the incorporation reaches for purposes of this closing condition is not stated here.

The condition calls for opinions "addressed to any of Moody's, S&P, the Indenture Trustee, the Owner Trustee, EMC, the Issuer, the Depositor and the Underwriter" and, in the same sentence, "addressed to the Insurer". Whether an opinion addressed only to another party satisfies the condition cannot be told from the text.

The condition fails if any proceeding "shall be pending or threatened", with no knowledge qualifier, no materiality threshold and no statement of who must perceive the threat. Any asserted threat of suit would literally defeat the condition.

The condition turns on the Underwriter's obligation "to purchase the Offered Notes", a term not defined in Article I or anywhere in this Agreement, though "Notes" and "Insured Notes" are both defined. Which classes the condition covers is left open.

The ratings condition requires that "the Notes that are rated, when issued, will be rated 'AAA' by S&P and 'Aaa' by Moody's", without identifying which classes are the rated Notes; the Class B Notes plainly would not carry those ratings. The self-selecting phrase "the Notes that are rated" makes the condition circular.

The condition is that "[n]o Default or Event of Default shall have occurred", omitting the "and is continuing" qualifier that Section 2.01(f) attaches to the identical representation. A cured Default would fail this condition but not that representation.

The condition is met only if the Insurer and its counsel "shall have reasonably determined" that all documents "conform to the terms" of five separate instruments, without saying what non-conformity matters. Both the standard of conformity and the reasonableness of the determination are unbounded.

The condition requires "evidence satisfactory to it" of delivery and endorsement, with satisfaction left wholly to the Insurer and no form of evidence specified. What discharges the condition is not ascertainable from the text.

Periodic rating agency fees are billed to "the Seller", a capitalized term that is defined nowhere in this Agreement, in the Policy or in the parties list, which uses "Sponsor", "Depositor" and "Issuer"; "Rating Agencies" is likewise undefined here. Who must pay the ongoing fees cannot be determined from the subsection.

The obligation is to pay fees "incurred by the Insurer in connection with the issuance of the Policy amounts and as described in the Premium Letter", a sentence whose words do not parse and which may mean either fees in the amounts described in the Premium Letter or fees of the kinds described there. The measure of what EMC owes at closing turns on the broken phrase.

The Premium is stated to be "fully earned by the Insurer as of the date of issuance" and nonrefundable, yet "payable in periodic installments of Premium Amounts as provided in the Premium Letter" and "in accordance with ... Section 3.02 of the Indenture". Whether the whole earned Premium becomes payable on early termination or redemption, or only installment by installment through the Indenture waterfall, is unresolved.

Reimbursement is expressed as arising "[a]s and when due in accordance with and from the funds specified in Section 3.02(a) of the Indenture", which can be read to confine the Insurer's reimbursement right to the Indenture waterfall, against Section 3.02(c) and the Article III indemnity obligations that make EMC directly liable to the Insurer. Whether reimbursement is a general obligation or a limited-recourse claim on trust funds is the collision.
